title: A Man, a Plan, a Canal—Mars!

sentences.en: This is 99% Invisible.
sentences.zh: 这里是百分之九十九隐形。

sentences.en: I'm Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 我是罗曼·马尔斯。

sentences.en: For centuries, humans have looked up into the night sky and wondered,
sentences.zh: 几个世纪以来，人类一直仰望夜空并思索，

sentences.en: are we alone in the universe?
sentences.zh: 我们在宇宙中是孤独的吗？

sentences.en: The possibility of intelligent life elsewhere in the cosmos
sentences.zh: 宇宙其他地方存在智慧生命的可能

sentences.en: remains one of the great mysteries,
sentences.zh: 仍然是最大的谜团之一，

sentences.en: and one that I don't expect to see resolved in my lifetime.
sentences.zh: 而且是我预计在有生之年看不到解开的谜团。

sentences.en: But for a brief period headed into the 20th century,
sentences.zh: 但在迈入20世纪的一段短暂时期内，

sentences.en: much of the Western world believed that this question,
sentences.zh: 西方世界的大部分人相信这个问题，

sentences.en: are we alone, had finally been answered.
sentences.zh: 我们在宇宙中是否孤独，终于有了答案。

sentences.en: Because we had discovered evidence of an advanced alien civilization living on Mars.
sentences.zh: 因为我们发现了火星上居住着高度发达的外星文明的证据。

sentences.en: Alexander Graham Bell wrote that he thought there was no question
sentences.zh: 亚历山大·格雷厄姆·贝尔写道，他认为毫无疑问
zh_words: 亚历山大·格雷厄姆·贝尔

sentences.en: that there was intelligent life on Mars.
sentences.zh: 火星上存在智慧生命。

sentences.en: There were, you know, professors at Harvard and Yale and Brown,
sentences.zh: 你知道的，当时有来自哈佛、耶鲁和布朗大学的教授，

sentences.en: Ivy League institutions, who were totally on board with this.
sentences.zh: 那些常春藤盟校，他们对这一观点深信不疑。

sentences.en: To the point where in the end of 1907,
sentences.zh: 以至于在1907年底，

sentences.en: the Wall Street Journal said the biggest news of the year
sentences.zh: 《华尔街日报》称年度最大新闻

sentences.en: was proof of intelligent life on Mars.
sentences.zh: 就是火星存在智慧生命的证据。

sentences.en: This is David Barron, a science journalist and author of a new book called
sentences.zh: 这是大卫·巴伦，一名科学记者兼新书的作者，

sentences.en: The Martians, the true story of an alien craze that captured turn-of-the-century America.
sentences.zh: 书名为《火星人》，讲述了一场迷倒世纪之交美国的真实外星人狂热。

sentences.en: David says that news of extraterrestrial life at that time permeated the culture.
sentences.zh: 大卫说，当时关于地外生命的新闻渗透到了整个文化中。

sentences.en: Martians were everywhere.
sentences.zh: 火星人无处不在。

sentences.en: You'd see Martians depicted in Broadway plays and vaudeville skits.
sentences.zh: 你会看到百老汇戏剧和杂耍小品中描绘的火星人。

sentences.en: There were songs about the Martians in Tin Pan Alley music.
sentences.zh: 廷潘阿利音乐中流传着关于火星人的歌曲。

sentences.en: There were Martians in advertising.
sentences.zh: 广告中也有火星人。

sentences.en: There was a Martian in the comics, a guy named Mr. Skygack from Mars,
sentences.zh: 漫画里甚至有个火星人，一个名叫来自火星的斯凯盖克先生的家伙，

sentences.en: who was in newspapers across the country.
sentences.zh: 他出现在全国各地的报纸上。

sentences.en: I recently spoke with David about his book,
sentences.zh: 我最近和大卫谈论了他的新书，

sentences.en: and so much of it still resonates with debates that we're having today
sentences.zh: 其中很多内容至今仍与我们今天正在进行的争论产生共鸣

sentences.en: about science, expertise, and truth.
sentences.zh: 关于科学、专业知识和真相。

sentences.en: The story he tells is one of mass delusion,
sentences.zh: 他讲述的故事是一个集体错觉的故事，

sentences.en: about the dangers of unchecked speculation seeping into public discourse.
sentences.zh: 关于未经核实的推测渗透到公众话语中的危险。

sentences.en: And it's a drama that centers around the misplaced ambitions
sentences.zh: 这是一场围绕着错误抱负展开的戏剧

sentences.en: of one wealthy amateur astronomer who convinced the world Martians were real.
sentences.zh: 主角是一位富有的业余天文学家，他让全世界相信火星人是真实的。

sentences.en: Here's my chat with David Barron.
sentences.zh: 以下是我与大卫·巴伦的对话。

sentences.en: So your book centers on a character named Percival Lowell,
sentences.zh: 所以你的书围绕着一个名叫珀西瓦尔·洛厄尔的角色展开，

sentences.en: and he's sort of the engine powering this idea of life on Mars.
sentences.zh: 他可以说是推动火星生命这一想法的发动机。

sentences.en: Could you talk about who Percival Lowell was?
sentences.zh: 能谈谈帕西瓦尔·洛厄尔是谁吗？

sentences.en: Well, so Lowell was an interesting man psychologically.
sentences.zh: 嗯，洛厄尔在心理上是一个很有趣的人。

sentences.en: Now, obviously, I never met him, and I'm not a psychoanalySt.
sentences.zh: 当然，我显然没见过他，我也不是心理分析师。

sentences.en: But, you know, he clearly had a big ego and a fragile ego.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道的，他显然既有极大的自我，又有着脆弱的自尊。

sentences.en: So Percival Lowell came from one of the most prominent families in New England.
sentences.zh: 帕西瓦尔·洛厄尔出身于新英格兰最显赫的家族之一。

sentences.en: The Lowells of Massachusetts were incredibly wealthy,
sentences.zh: 马萨诸塞州的洛厄尔家族极其富有，

sentences.en: were big philanthropists, were big in the culture of Massachusetts and the United States.
sentences.zh: 是大慈善家，在马萨诸塞州乃至美国的文化界都举足轻重。

sentences.en: Percival graduated from Harvard, like all the men in the family did.
sentences.zh: 帕西瓦尔毕业于哈佛大学，家族里的所有男性都是如此。

sentences.en: He was the eldest son.
sentences.zh: 他是长子。

sentences.en: And he had a lot of weight on his shoulders.
sentences.zh: 他肩负着沉重的压力。

sentences.en: He was a Lowell.
sentences.zh: 他是个洛厄尔。

sentences.en: His father had told him and his brother that they had to do something important with their lives.
sentences.zh: 他的父亲曾对他和他的兄弟说，他们必须在有生之年做成一些重要的事情。

sentences.en: And so for a while he traveled.
sentences.zh: 因此，他有一段时间到处旅行。

sentences.en: He was a writer.
sentences.zh: 他曾是一名作家。

sentences.en: He was one of the very first Americans to go to Korea.
sentences.zh: 他是最早去朝鲜的美国人之一。

sentences.en: He wrote a book about it.
sentences.zh: 他写了一本关于那里的书。

sentences.en: So he really made quite a name for himself as this kind of roving anthropologiSt.
sentences.zh: 因此，他作为这种四处游历的人类学家，确实让自己名声大噪。

sentences.en: But as he approached the age of 40, he decided he wanted to become an astronomer.
sentences.zh: 但当他接近40岁时，他决定成为一名天文学家。

sentences.en: And he had the wealth to do it in a big way.
sentences.zh: 而且他有足够的财富大干一场。

sentences.en: And he really, he became, in essence, the most famous astronomer of that time in America.
sentences.zh: 他真的，从本质上讲，成为了当时美国最著名的天文学家。

sentences.en: And so when Lowell takes up astronomy, like, what is going on in the field?
sentences.zh: 那么，当洛厄尔开始从事天文学研究时，这一领域正在发生什么？

sentences.en: And maybe more specifically, what was going on with Mars?
sentences.zh: 或者说得更具体一点，火星当时是什么情况？

sentences.en: So there were big advances in astronomy in the 19th century.
sentences.zh: 因此，19世纪的天文学取得了巨大的进展。

sentences.en: Telescopes were now getting quite large and sophisticated.
sentences.zh: 望远镜现在变得相当大型且精密。

sentences.en: And so astronomers by the late 19th century were getting a really good view of the surface of Mars.
sentences.zh: 因此，到19世纪后期，天文学家们对火星表面的观察已经非常清晰。

sentences.en: Now Mars, of course, is right next to us in terms of its orbit.
sentences.zh: 当然，就轨道而言，火星就在我们隔壁。

sentences.en: But Earth and Mars only come close together once every 26 months.
sentences.zh: 但地球和火星每26个月才会接近一次。

sentences.en: And about every 15 years, Earth and Mars come especially close together.
sentences.zh: 大约每15年，地球和火星会靠得格外近。

sentences.en: And that's the time when you can really get a, through your telescope, see Mars in relatively good detail.
sentences.zh: 那是你真正能够通过望远镜相对看清火星细节的时期。

sentences.en: Well, 1877 was one of those years.
sentences.zh: 而1877年就是这样的年份之一。

sentences.en: And there was an astronomer in Milan named Giovanni Schiaparelli who decided he was going to create a new map of Mars.
sentences.zh: 米兰有一位名叫乔瓦尼·斯基亚帕雷利的天文学家，他决定绘制一张新的火星地图。

sentences.en: And night after night, he studied the planet and he drew what he saw with precision.
sentences.zh: 他夜复一夜地研究这颗行星，并将他所看到的精确地画了下来。

sentences.en: And when he came out with this map, Mars, first of all, looked very Earth-like.
sentences.zh: 当他发布这张地图时，火星首先看起来非常像地球。

sentences.en: It had dark areas that were assumed to be oceans and light areas that were thought to be continents.
sentences.zh: 它有被认为是海洋的暗色区域，也有被认为是大陆的明亮区域。

sentences.en: But Schiaparelli also saw these fine lines crisscrossing the light areas.
sentences.zh: 但斯基亚帕雷利还看到这些细小的线条纵横交错在明亮的区域上。

sentences.en: And he imagined that they were waterways of some sort.
sentences.zh: 他想象它们某种程度上是水道。

sentences.en: So he called them canali, which in Italian means channels.
sentences.zh: 所以他称它们为canali，在意大利语中意思是海峡或沟渠。

sentences.en: They were water channels of some sort.
sentences.zh: 它们是某种水路。

sentences.en: Well, canali was translated or mistranslated into English as canals, which has a very different meaning.
sentences.zh: 嗯，“canali”在英语中被翻译或误译为了 canals（运河），这有着非常不同的含义。

sentences.en: Meaning.
sentences.zh: 意思是。

sentences.en: Yeah, like a channel or waterway is naturally occurring in the landscape.
sentences.zh: 对，就像是自然存在于地貌中的河道或水道。

sentences.en: But a canal, like that's made by something or someone.
sentences.zh: 但运河，就像是由某物或某人建造的那种。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: They were a mystery.
sentences.zh: 它们曾是个谜。

sentences.en: No one knew what these lines that looked so straight that they seemed artificial might be.
sentences.zh: 没有人知道这些看起来笔直得似乎是人工制造的线条可能是什么。

sentences.en: And it was Percival Lowell when he decided in 1894 to dedicate the next stage of his life to studying Mars, to becoming an astronomer.
sentences.zh: 正是在1894年，帕西瓦尔·洛厄尔决定将他人生的下一个阶段奉献给火星研究，致力于成为一名天文学家。

sentences.en: And he was going to solve the mystery of the canals.
sentences.zh: 而他打算解开运河之谜。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And Lowell ultimately comes up with this grand theory.
sentences.zh: 最终，洛厄尔提出了这个宏大的理论。

sentences.en: He says not only are the canals real, but in fact, they're a massive planet-wide system created by an advanced alien civilization living on Mars, which is like crazy.
sentences.zh: 他说这些运河不仅是真实的，而且事实上，它们是由生活在火星上的一个高级外星文明所创造的横跨整个星球的庞大系统，这听起来太疯狂了。

sentences.en: But could you explain his thinking at the time?
sentences.zh: 但你能解释一下他当时的想法吗？

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: So I know that today it sounds ridiculous.
sentences.zh: 所以我知道这在今天听起来很荒谬。

sentences.en: How could anyone take this seriously?
sentences.zh: 怎么会有人把这当真呢？

sentences.en: But it was—I actually give him credit.
sentences.zh: 但它——我其实挺佩服他的。

sentences.en: It was a coherent theory that fit with a lot of ideas about Mars at the time that at least was worth investigating.
sentences.zh: 这是一个连贯的理论，它符合当时关于火星的许多想法，至少是值得研究的。

sentences.en: So here was the theory.
sentences.zh: 所以理论是这样的。

sentences.en: Mars, it was widely believed, was an older planet than Earth.
sentences.zh: 人们普遍认为，火星是一颗比地球更古老的行星。

sentences.en: So Mars hardened and became habitable before Earth did.
sentences.zh: 因此，火星比地球更早冷却固化并变得宜居。

sentences.en: So you might imagine that there was life on Mars before on Earth, that life on Mars became intelligent before life on Earth.
sentences.zh: 所以你可以想象，火星上的生命出现得比地球早，火星上的生命比地球上的生命更早变得具有智慧。

sentences.en: So now Mars, it was thought, was in its dying phases.
sentences.zh: 人们认为，现在的火星正处于其消亡阶段。

sentences.en: And it was known that Mars had polar ice caps.
sentences.zh: 而且众所周知，火星有极冠冰盖。

sentences.en: So if, in fact, there was intelligent life on Mars and the water was running out, well,
sentences.zh: 所以，如果火星上真的有智慧生命，并且水快用完了，那么，

sentences.en: what you would need to do was tap the meltwater from the ice cap and bring the water down to where your cities and your farms are.
sentences.zh: 你需要做的事情就是利用冰盖融水，把水引到你的城市和农场所在地。

sentences.en: That's what he thought the canals were.
sentences.zh: 这就是他认为运河的作用。

sentences.en: This was a worldwide irrigation network that allowed the Martians to survive off the water from the ice caps.
sentences.zh: 这是一个全球性的灌溉网络，使火星人能够靠冰盖的水生存下去。

sentences.en: So it was a coherent theory, but, you know, he went into it wanting to prove himself right, which is kind of a mistake in science.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个连贯的理论，但是，你知道的，他带着证明自己是对的的动机去研究它，这在科学中算是一个错误。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And Lowell, of course, has a lot of time and money at his disposal to prove himself right.
sentences.zh: 而且，洛厄尔当然有大量的精力和资金供他挥霍来证明自己是对的。

sentences.en: So one of the first things he does is build this state-of-the-art observatory out in Flagstaff, Arizona.
sentences.zh: 所以他做的第一件事就是在亚利桑那州弗拉格斯塔夫建造了这个最先进的天文台。

sentences.en: And he starts looking at Mars through his big, expensive telescope and then drawing what he sees.
sentences.zh: 他开始通过他那台昂贵的大型望远镜观测火星，并画下他所看到的东西。

sentences.en: But for Lowell, could you describe what are the obstacles of trying to look at the surface of Mars back in the 1800s?
sentences.zh: 但对洛厄尔来说，你能描述一下在19世纪尝试观测火星表面时有哪些障碍吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I mean, we have to put out of our minds everything we know about Mars today because we've all seen high-resolution photos and videos of the surface of Mars.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我们必须抛开我们今天对火星所知的一切，因为我们都见过火星表面的高分辨率照片和视频。

sentences.en: We know what it looks like.
sentences.zh: 我们知道它长什么样。

sentences.en: But cast yourself back into the late 19th century,
sentences.zh: 但如果你把思绪拉回到19世纪末期，

sentences.en: all we knew about Mars was what you could see through an Earth-bound telescope of a planet that at its closest is 35 million miles away.
sentences.zh: 我们对火星的全部认知，仅限于通过地球上的望远镜去观察一颗在最近时距离地球也有3500万英里远的行星。

sentences.en: But more than that, you're looking through the Earth's atmosphere.
sentences.zh: 不仅如此，你还得透过地球的大气层去观察。

sentences.en: It's like looking at the sky from the bottom of the ocean.
sentences.zh: 这就好比在海底仰望星空。

sentences.en: This ocean of air distorts the light as it comes in.
sentences.zh: 这层气态海洋会扭曲穿透而来的光线。

sentences.en: And so looking at Mars, even through a fine telescope, it tends to go in and out of focus.
sentences.zh: 因此观察火星时，哪怕是通过优质的望远镜，影像也往往会时而清晰时而模糊。

sentences.en: It wobbles.
sentences.zh: 它在晃动。

sentences.en: So you only have often just split-second glimpses of clarity.
sentences.zh: 所以你往往只有电光石火般清晰的瞬间。

sentences.en: So you have to stare at the planet over long, long periods to get these moments of clarity and then remember what you saw.
sentences.zh: 因此你必须长时间、坚持不懈地盯着这颗行星，才能捕捉到这些清晰的时刻，然后记住你所看到的一切。

sentences.en: And so those canals, it's not like you could stare at the planet and you would just see this whole array of canals.
sentences.zh: 所以关于那些运河，并不是说你能盯着火星，就能一眼看到整片运河网。

sentences.en: No, you would see this fuzzy orange-red orb in your telescope wobbling around.
sentences.zh: 不，你在望远镜里看到的只会是一个模糊的橙红色球体在晃来晃去。

sentences.en: And then suddenly you'd see a little bit came into focus and, oh, I saw some lines.
sentences.zh: 然后突然间你看到有一小部分变得清晰了，哦，我看到一些线条了。

sentences.en: And you draw those.
sentences.zh: 接着你把它们画下来。

sentences.en: And then you stare some more and you see more of these lines.
sentences.zh: 然后你继续盯着看，又看到了更多这样的线条。

sentences.en: So it was very, very difficult to really get a sense of what was there.
sentences.zh: 所以要想真正弄清楚那里有什么，是非常非常困难的。

sentences.en: And in the book, you actually write about going to Lowell's observatory yourself.
sentences.zh: 你在书中确实写到了自己亲自去罗威尔天文台的经历。

sentences.en: I did, actually.
sentences.zh: 我的确去了。

sentences.en: So in 2018, I went to the Lowell Observatory in Flagstaff to look through Lowell's very telescope at a time when Mars and Earth were exceptionally close.
sentences.zh: 所以在2018年，我去了弗拉格斯塔夫的罗威尔天文台，透过罗威尔的望远镜亲自观察，当时火星和地球正处于极其接近的位置。

sentences.en: And just staring at this apricot-colored orb in the telescope, it really is sort of hypnotic.
sentences.zh: 就那样凝视着望远镜里这个杏黄色的球体，真的有种催眠般的感觉。

sentences.en: You just – you stare and you stare and you stare.
sentences.zh: 你只是——你一直盯着，一直盯着，一直盯着。

sentences.en: And it's sometimes hard to know what you've seen and what you thought you saw, what you imagined you saw.
sentences.zh: 有时很难分清你究竟看到了什么，你以为自己看到了什么，以及你凭想象看到了什么。

sentences.en: And is he working with other folks that are sort of buttressing his claims or what is – is he alone in this field?
sentences.zh: 那他当时有没有和其他一些支持他观点的人合作，还是说——他在这个领域是孤军奋战？

sentences.en: Well, so he had – when he established the Lowell Observatory, he actually hired away a couple of Harvard astronomers to help him first found the observatory.
sentences.zh: 嗯，所以他——当他建立罗威尔天文台时，他实际上挖来了几位哈佛的天文学家来帮他首先建立天文台。

sentences.en: And then he kept one on his staff.
sentences.zh: 然后他留用了一位在自己的员工团队里。

sentences.en: And so this assistant of his, who was a fine astronomer named Andrew Ellicott Douglas, A.E.
sentences.zh: 所以这位他的助手，是一位出色的天文学家，名叫安德鲁·埃利科特·道格拉斯，也就是A.E.
zh_words: 安德鲁·埃利科特·道格拉斯

sentences.en: Douglas, you know, he went along with his boss.
sentences.zh: 道格拉斯，你知道的，他一直顺从着他的老板。

sentences.en: He saw the lines too.
sentences.zh: 他也看到了这些线条。

sentences.en: He mapped the lines.
sentences.zh: 他还把这些线条绘制成了地图。

sentences.en: But over time, he started to question whether the lines were real or if they were illusory.
sentences.zh: 但随着时间的推移，他开始怀疑这些线条究竟是真实的，还是只是幻觉。

sentences.en: And as soon as he expressed any doubt about it, Lowell summarily fired him, which says a lot about Lowell that he did not like to be questioned.
sentences.zh: 而他一旦流露出任何怀疑，罗威尔就立刻把他解雇了，这充分说明罗威尔是个不喜欢被人质疑的人。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So when Percival Lowell sees these channels, which he posits are canals, are they immediately accepted as a thing in the scientific community or is there a debate about them?
sentences.zh: 那么当珀西瓦尔·罗威尔看到这些他认为是人工运河的沟渠时，科学界是立刻就接受了这一说法，还是对此展开了争论？

sentences.en: Oh, there was huge debate.
sentences.zh: 哦，引发了巨大的争论。

sentences.en: So these lines on Mars, these canals on Mars, were very hard to see.
sentences.zh: 所以火星上的这些线条，火星上的这些运河，其实非常难看清。

sentences.en: You know, there were astronomers at other observatories with excellent telescopes who didn't see the lines.
sentences.zh: 你知道，其他天文台拥有极佳望远镜的天文学家并没有看到这些线条。

sentences.en: And even Schiaparelli said they're not always there.
sentences.zh: 就连斯基帕雷利也说过，它们并不总是存在。

sentences.en: You don't always see them.
sentences.zh: 你并非总是能看到它们。

sentences.en: You have to have the right viewing conditions.
sentences.zh: 你必须具备适宜的观测条件才行。

sentences.en: And to make it even more complicated, the lines came and went.
sentences.zh: 更复杂的是，这些线条还会时隐时现。

sentences.en: So it seemed that they came and went with the seasons on Mars.
sentences.zh: 所以看起来它们是随着火星的季节而出现和消失的。

sentences.en: It was all very mysterious.
sentences.zh: 这一切都非常神秘。

sentences.en: But, you know, when you have one astronomer saying, I don't see them, and another who says, I do.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，当一个天文学家说“我没看到”，而另一个说“我看到了”。

sentences.en: Well, the one who doesn't see them, you can say, well, your eyesight isn't good enough.
sentences.zh: 好吧，对于那个没看到的人，你可以说，嗯，你的视力不够好。

sentences.en: Your telescope isn't good enough.
sentences.zh: 你的望远镜不够好。

sentences.en: Your observatory is located in a place with bad air overhead that you can't really get a clear view of Mars.
sentences.zh: 你的天文台建在一个头顶大气条件很差的地方，导致你无法真正看清火星。

sentences.en: So those who saw them kind of had the upper hand against those who didn't see them.
sentences.zh: 所以，那些看到这些线条的人在与没看到的人争论时，往往占了上风。

sentences.en: And so how does Lowell ultimately start pushing his grand theory out to the public?
sentences.zh: 那么，洛厄尔究竟是如何开始向公众大力推行他的宏大理论的呢？

sentences.en: So Lowell was incredibly articulate.
sentences.zh: 洛厄尔口才极佳。

sentences.en: He was considered an excellent speaker.
sentences.zh: 他被认为是一位优秀的演说家。

sentences.en: He came from a prominent family.
sentences.zh: 他出身名门望族。

sentences.en: People would listen to him.
sentences.zh: 人们愿意听他讲话。

sentences.en: He had all sorts of means of conveying his ideas.
sentences.zh: 他拥有各种各样传达自己想法的途径。

sentences.en: So first of all, in Boston at the time, there was a popular organization called the Lowell Institute, which brought in prominent speakers to give free lectures to the public.
sentences.zh: 首先，当时在波士顿有一个名为洛厄尔研究所的受欢迎组织，该组织邀请知名演讲者为公众举办免费讲座。

sentences.en: And, of course, this was founded by one of his late cousins.
sentences.zh: 当然，这是由他的一位已故表亲创立的。

sentences.en: In fact, it was overseen by Lowell's very father.
sentences.zh: 事实上，它一直由洛厄尔的亲生父亲监管。

sentences.en: Lowell was invited to speak about Mars to the Lowell Institute, which actually had its lectures in a room, a big auditorium at MIT.
sentences.zh: 洛厄尔应邀在洛厄尔研究所发表关于火星的演讲，该研究所的讲座实际上是在麻省理工学院的一个大礼堂里进行的。

sentences.en: So he reached audiences that way.
sentences.zh: 就这样，他接触到了广大受众。

sentences.en: Lowell then published the text of his talks in the Atlantic Monthly.
sentences.zh: 洛厄尔随后在《大西洋月刊》上发表了他的演讲文稿。

sentences.en: The founding editor of the Atlantic Monthly was James Russell Lowell, also a relative.
sentences.zh: 《大西洋月刊》的创办编辑正是詹姆斯·拉塞尔·洛厄尔，他也是个亲戚。

sentences.en: And so he was very good at presenting his ideas to the public.
sentences.zh: 因此，他非常擅长向公众表达自己的想法。

sentences.en: And it doesn't take long before you have a few lectures,
sentences.zh: 没过多久，你就会做几次演讲，

sentences.en: you have a few articles in the Atlantic that journalism he's not connected to just like takes this up and is very excited by these ideas.
sentences.zh: 你在《大西洋月刊》上发表了几篇文章，那些与他没有直接关联的新闻界也纷纷关注并对这些想法感到非常兴奋。

sentences.en: Can you talk about what the papers were like at this time and how they kind of used the Mars craze to sell papers?
sentences.zh: 你能谈谈当时报纸是什么样的，以及它们是如何利用火星热来卖报纸的吗？

sentences.en: So this was a time when there was a revolution underway in America's newspapers.
sentences.zh: 因此，这是一个美国报业正在经历革命的时代。

sentences.en: So the famous publishers, Joseph Pulitzer and William Randolph Hearst, were basically inventing the tabloid press, which at the time was called the Yellow Press.
sentences.zh: 著名的出版商约瑟夫·普利策和威廉·伦道夫·赫斯特基本上发明了小报新闻，当时被称为黄色新闻。

sentences.en: And they latched on to anything that was sensationalistic.
sentences.zh: 而且他们抓住任何耸人听闻的东西不放。

sentences.en: Well, the idea of life on Mars fit right in.
sentences.zh: 嗯，火星上有生命的想法正合他们的心意。

sentences.en: And so the Pulitzer and Hearst newspapers, when there was talk of the Martians, they really pushed it out onto the public.
sentences.zh: 因此，普利策和赫斯特的报纸在听到关于火星人的传言时，便极力将其向公众推波助澜。

sentences.en: And they latched on to what Lowell was saying.
sentences.zh: 而且他们抓住了洛厄尔所说的话不放。

sentences.en: And so that helped to propel this idea out into the general populace.
sentences.zh: 这有助于将这个概念推向广大民众。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: And beyond the press, other prominent scientists and academics are really pushing Lowell's theory, too, including Nikola Tesla.
sentences.zh: 除了媒体，其他一些杰出的科学家和学者也 realmente 在大力推崇洛厄尔的理论，其中就包括尼古拉·特斯拉。

sentences.en: So how does he fit into all this?
sentences.zh: 那么他怎么切入这一切的？

sentences.en: So Nikola Tesla was a genius who changed the world.
sentences.zh: 尼古拉·特斯拉是一个改变了世界的天才。

sentences.en: He also was an eccentric guy.
sentences.zh: 他同时也是一个古怪的人。

sentences.en: And in 1899, after having done all this work with the distribution of electricity by wires, he was getting interested in what was called wireless, what today we would call radio.
sentences.zh: 在1899年，在完成了所有这些通过电线输电的工作后，他开始对所谓的无线电感兴趣，也就是我们今天所说的无线电。

sentences.en: And so he set up an experimental laboratory in Colorado in 1899 to study how electrical waves were transmitted through the atmosphere.
sentences.zh: 因此，他在1899年在科罗拉多建立了一个实验实验室，以研究电波是如何通过大气传播的。

sentences.en: This was before there was anything, there were no radio stations, but you could listen to natural electromagnetic radiation, like from lightning.
sentences.zh: 这在任何东西出现之前就已经开始了，当时没有任何广播电台，但你可以听到自然的电磁辐射，比如来自闪电的辐射。

sentences.en: And Tesla, one night alone in the lab, was listening to the sounds of distant lightning and other things.
sentences.zh: 一天晚上，特斯拉独自在实验室里，聆听着远处的闪电和其他事物的声音。

sentences.en: And he heard the weirdest thing in his receiver.
sentences.zh: 他在接收器里听到了一件最奇怪的事。

sentences.en: It was this signal that repeated in triplets.
sentences.zh: 这是一个以三连音重复的信号。

sentences.en: It was sort of a click, click, click, click, click, click, click, over and over again.
sentences.zh: 这有点像咔哒、咔哒、咔哒、咔哒、咔哒、咔哒、咔哒，一遍又一遍。

sentences.en: And he pondered for a while what could possibly be causing it.
sentences.zh: 他思索了一会儿，究竟是什么原因导致了这一切。

sentences.en: And Tesla eventually decided there was no natural explanation.
sentences.zh: 特斯拉最终认为，这没有自然的解释。

sentences.en: The most logical explanation was this was Percival Lowell's Martians sending a signal to the Earth.
sentences.zh: 最符合逻辑的解释是，这是帕西瓦尔·洛厄尔的火星人在向地球发送信号。

sentences.en: And when Tesla announced this to the world, the craze just completely took off.
sentences.zh: 当特斯拉向世界宣布这一点时，这股狂热彻底爆发了。

sentences.en: And one of the things that you do in the book is sort of cast yourself back to this time period.
sentences.zh: 你在书中做的事情之一，就是把自己带回到那个时代。

sentences.en: And you flat out say that you probably would have gotten wrapped up in this craze around Mars, too.
sentences.zh: 而且你直言不讳地说，你当时可能也会卷入这场围绕火星的狂热之中。

sentences.en: So can you can you talk a little bit about that?
sentences.zh: 所以你能谈谈这件事吗？

sentences.en: Like what is happening around the turn of the century that made life on Mars feel like it made complete sense?
sentences.zh: 比如，在世纪之交发生了什么，让人们觉得火星上有生命是完全说得通的？

sentences.en: Well, so this was the period that today we remember as the Gilded Age, which makes it sound like it was this glittering, wonderful time.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这个时期我们今天被称为镀金时代，这听起来像是一个闪耀、美好的时代。

sentences.en: It really wasn't for many, many people, right?
sentences.zh: 对许许多多的人来说，事实并非如此，对吧？

sentences.en: We know that there was this tremendous divide between the few exceptionally rich and the many who were desperately poor.
sentences.zh: 我们知道，极少数极其富有的人和绝大多数极度贫困的人之间存在着巨大的鸿沟。

sentences.en: This was a time when there was violent labor unrest, when there was anarchism.
sentences.zh: 那是一个充满激烈的劳资动乱和无政府主义的时代。

sentences.en: William McKinley, President William McKinley, was assassinated by an anarchist in the United States.
sentences.zh: 威廉·麦金莱，麦金莱总统，在美国遭到了一名无政府主义者的暗杀。

sentences.en: So there was a sense that the world was falling apart, that things were not going so well on Earth.
sentences.zh: 因此，当时有一种世界正在瓦解的感觉，觉得地球上的事情进展得并不那么顺利。

sentences.en: And part of the of Percival Lowell's theory was that the Martians were not only in advance of us intellectually and in terms of their technology,
sentences.zh: 珀西瓦尔·洛厄尔理论的一部分是，火星人不仅在智力和技术上领先于我们，

sentences.en: but they were better than us morally.
sentences.zh: 而且在道德上也比我们更崇高。

sentences.en: After all, if the planet has developed this global irrigation network, that means everyone everywhere is working together.
sentences.zh: 毕竟，如果这颗行星已经建设了这样一个全球性的灌溉网络，那就意味着无处不在的每个人都在齐心协力。

sentences.en: The the Martians up in the Arctic are working together with those in the equator, that there there must not be warring nations.
sentences.zh: 北极的火星人正在与赤道的火星人通力合作，那里一定没有交战的国度。

sentences.en: This is an entire planet that's pulled together as one.
sentences.zh: 这是一个团结如一的完整星球。

sentences.en: And that was a very appealing notion to people at that time to think that, well, maybe there maybe it's possible to create a world where there's less violence,
sentences.zh: 对于当时的人们来说，这是一个极具吸引力的想法，他们会想，也许，也许有可能创造一个暴力更少的世界，

sentences.en: where people are where beings are working together.
sentences.zh: 一个人们、一个众生都在齐心协力的世界。

sentences.en: And more than that, if we could just get in touch with the Martians, maybe they could solve our problems here on Earth.
sentences.zh: 不仅如此，如果我们能与火星人取得联系，也许他们能解决我们地球上的问题。

sentences.en: You know, I think if you were to tell people today that there was evidence of intelligent life in the universe, and I think people think about it as like, well,
sentences.zh: 你知道，我想如果你今天告诉人们宇宙中存在智能生命的证据，我认为人们会觉得，嗯，

sentences.en: if we had evidence of that, it would be so like earth shaking to everything we believe would upend theology.
sentences.zh: 如果我们有了这样的证据，它将是如此震撼地球，以至于我们所相信的一切都会颠覆神学。

sentences.en: It would upend our sense of self in the in the universe, our sense of science.
sentences.zh: 它会颠覆我们在宇宙中的自我认知，颠覆我们的科学认知。

sentences.en: And we actually went through this where people mostly believe this, and it seems like it didn't have that type of effect where it upended everything.
sentences.zh: 而我们实际上经历过这种情况，当时人们大多相信这一点，但它似乎并没有产生那种颠覆一切的影响。

sentences.en: It really just sort of like it kind of fit in nicely with everyone's view of God and religion and science.
sentences.zh: 它真的只是很好地契合了每个人对上帝、宗教和科学的看法。

sentences.en: Could you talk about that, like how much it was so kind of nicely metabolized into our worldview?
sentences.zh: 你能谈谈这个吗，比如它是如何如此完美地融入我们的世界观的？

sentences.en: Yeah, I mean, that really surprised me because you would think that, and there were people at the time speculating that this would cause traditional religion to crumble.
sentences.zh: 是的，我是说，这真的让我很惊讶，因为你会这么想，当时确实有人推测这会导致传统宗教崩溃。

sentences.en: I mean, you know, if Christ came to Earth to save our souls, did Christ go to Mars too?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你知道，如果基督来到地球拯救我们的灵魂，那基督也去过火星吗？

sentences.en: I mean, that seems to be stretching things.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，那似乎有点太勉强了。

sentences.en: Um, but actually, no, theologians and clergy were able to incorporate these ideas and not really, they didn't feel that it undermined their beliefs.
sentences.zh: 嗯，但实际上，并没有，神学家和神职人员能够将这些思想融入其中，而且实际上，他们并不觉得这动摇了他们的信仰。

sentences.en: And if anything, they found ways for it to amplify their beliefs.
sentences.zh: 如果说有什么不同的话，他们找到了让这些思想升华信仰的方法。

sentences.en: This was just even more worlds, more beings for God to oversee.
sentences.zh: 这只是意味着有更多的世界，更多的生灵需要上帝去照看。

sentences.en: And it just showed the glory of God to be even greater than we imagined.
sentences.zh: 而且它恰恰展示了上帝的荣耀比我们想象的还要伟大。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So it isn't just like the gee whiz aspect of Martian life.
sentences.zh: 所以这不仅仅是火星生命那种让人惊叹的层面。

sentences.en: It really is about hope and how we want our, you know, the world to be.
sentences.zh: 它真正关乎的是希望，以及我们希望我们的世界，你知道的，变成什么样。

sentences.en: Well, that was one of the big, deep discoveries I felt that I made in studying that period.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我觉得那是我在研究那个时期时，得到的重大而深刻的发现之一。

sentences.en: Because I first went into it thinking, this is just, this is a rollicking good tale.
sentences.zh: 因为我一开始去研究的时候以为，这只是一段妙趣横生的好故事。

sentences.en: I mean, can you believe it, that at that time people really believed that they were Martians?
sentences.zh: 我是说，你怎么能相信，当时人们真的相信他们是火星人？

sentences.en: But then I came to see that it spoke to some very deep, universal desires of all of us.
sentences.zh: 但后来我开始明白，它触及了我们所有人内心深处的一些普遍渴望。

sentences.en: And this really, this really became clear when I found this newspaper article that ran across the country, many newspapers in 1909.
sentences.zh: 这一点在1909年全国许多报纸上刊登的一篇报纸文章中变得非常清晰。

sentences.en: At a time when there was serious discussion of coming up with a way to communicate with Mars.
sentences.zh: 当时人们正严肃讨论寻找与火星沟通的方法。

sentences.en: And so this article, the headline was, questions Mars might answer.
sentences.zh: 所以这篇文章，标题是，火星可能会解答的问题。

sentences.en: So it was a list of what we should ask the Martians when we finally get in touch with them.
sentences.zh: 所以它是一份列出当我们终于与火星人取得联系时应该问他们什么问题的清单。

sentences.en: Well, you would think we would ask them practical questions about building canals or, or maybe how to improve on the airplane of the Wright brothers.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你可能会认为我们会问他们关于建造运河的实际问题，或者，也许是如何改进莱特兄弟的飞机。

sentences.en: Because surely the Martians are far in advance of us when it comes to motorized flight.
sentences.zh: 因为在机动飞行方面，火星人肯定远远领先于我们。

sentences.en: No, the questions that were suggested for us to ask Mars were the most existential questions.
sentences.zh: 不，建议我们问火星的问题都是最具存在主义意义的问题。

sentences.en: What is the meaning of life?
sentences.zh: 人生的意义是什么？

sentences.en: What happens to the soul when you die?
sentences.zh: 人死后灵魂会怎样？

sentences.en: How can we prevent human suffering?
sentences.zh: 我们该如何阻止人类的苦难？

sentences.en: These were the questions we had for the Martians.
sentences.zh: 这些是我们想问火星人的问题。

sentences.en: After the break, the Mars fever breaks.
sentences.zh: 广告之后，火星狂热将告一段落。

sentences.en: And why this story still resonates today.
sentences.zh: 以及为什么这个故事在今天仍然能引起共鸣。

sentences.en: Stick around.
sentences.zh: 请继续收看。

sentences.en: We are back with David Barron.
sentences.zh: 我们请回了大卫·巴伦。

sentences.en: So at the turn of the century, Lowell's ideas about Mars are at the peak of their powers.
sentences.zh: 所以在世纪之交，洛厄尔关于火星的观点达到了其影响力的顶峰。

sentences.en: But pretty soon, more traditional astronomers see this popularity and they just decide it's time to finally put an end to all this craziness.
sentences.zh: 但很快，更传统的天文学家们看到了这种受欢迎程度，他们决定是时候彻底结束这场疯狂了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So among the anti-Canalists, there were those who said, these lines on Mars are nothing more than optical illusions.
sentences.zh: 所以在反运河派中，有人说，火星上的这些线条只不过是光学错觉。

sentences.en: It's the fact that we're looking at a planet at the very limit of our perception.
sentences.zh: 这是因为我们正在观察一颗处于我们感知极限的行星。

sentences.en: The eye is connecting up dots and seeing lines where there aren't any.
sentences.zh: 人类的眼睛把点连接起来，在根本没有线条的地方看到了线条。

sentences.en: And so one of the most prominent of these anti-Canalists was Edward Walter Maunder, who was an astronomer at the Greenwich Observatory in London.
sentences.zh: 因此，这些反对“运河说”的最著名代表人物之一，就是伦敦格林威治天文台的天文学家爱德华·沃尔特·蒙德。

sentences.en: And he came up with a really interesting experiment to see if this could be true.
sentences.zh: 他提出了一个非常有趣的实验，来验证这是否可能是真的。

sentences.en: He actually recruited these children, these young teens, at a boys' school right near the observatory to take part in an experiment where he took a map of Mars.
sentences.zh: 他实际上在天文台附近的一所男子学校招募了这些儿童和青少年，让他们参与一项实验：他拿来一张火星地图，

sentences.en: And where there were canals, he erased the canals, so he erased the straight lines and replaced them with meandering rivers or just stippling and shading,
sentences.zh: 在有运河的地方，他擦掉了运河，也就是说，他擦掉了直线，换成了蜿蜒的河流，或者仅仅是点画和阴影，

sentences.en: things that would be natural, not just a straight irrigation canal.
sentences.zh: 那些看起来很自然的东西，而不仅仅是笔直的灌溉运河。

sentences.en: And he had these depictions hung at the front of the classroom, and the boys were instructed to stay in their seats.
sentences.zh: 他在教室的前方挂上了这些画像，并指示男孩们呆在自己的座位上。

sentences.en: They couldn't go any closer for a better look from where they were to draw what they saw at the front of the room.
sentences.zh: 从他们所在的位置，他们不能走得更近去看个清楚，只能去画他们在教室前方看到的东西。

sentences.en: They didn't know it was a map of Mars.
sentences.zh: 他们不知道这是一张火星地图。

sentences.en: They had no idea what they were doing.
sentences.zh: 他们根本不知道自己在做什么。

sentences.en: They were just asked to draw it as faithfully as possible.
sentences.zh: 他们只是被要求尽可能忠实地把它画下来。

sentences.en: Well, it was really interesting.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这真的很有趣。

sentences.en: Those in the front of the room who could see the drawing very clearly drew it accurately with meandering rivers and stippling.
sentences.zh: 坐在教室前排能非常清楚地看到那张图的人，把蜿蜒的河流和点画都准确地画了下来。

sentences.en: Those in the very back of the room who were so far away, they really couldn't make out any of the details at all, left those features out entirely.
sentences.zh: 坐在教室最后排的人离得太远了，根本看不清任何细节，结果把那些特征完全漏掉了。

sentences.en: The boys in the middle of the room where they could see that there were some fine features but didn't know what they were, drew straight lines.
sentences.zh: 坐在教室中间的男孩们能看到有一些微小的特征却不知道那是什么，于是画了直线。

sentences.en: They were seeing those very illusions.
sentences.zh: 他们看到的正是那些错觉。

sentences.en: And so this then became, Lowell called it derisively, the small boy theory of the lines on Mars, which he said, well, how can you trust these Greenwich schoolboys?
sentences.zh: 于是这后来成了——洛厄尔讽刺地称之为火星线条的小男孩理论，他说，嗯，你怎么能信任这些格林威治的男校学生呢？

sentences.en: Over an accomplished astronomer like me, I can tell the difference between an illusion and what's real.
sentences.zh: 比起我这样一位有成就的天文学家，我能分辨出幻觉和真实之间的区别。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: He had just enough magnification to see something.
sentences.zh: 他的放大倍数刚好能看到一些东西。

sentences.en: And therefore, he started connecting the dots himself and drawing canals.
sentences.zh: 因此，他开始自己把这些点连起来并画出运河。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And so in fact, and what Monder, the astronomer who did the study,
sentences.zh: 事实上，进行这项研究的天文学家蒙德尔，

sentences.en: said was he thought that the reason no one had seen the canals on Mars until the late 19th century was because the telescopes weren't big enough and good enough.
sentences.zh: 曾说过他认为，直到19世纪晚期才有人看到火星上的运河，是因为当时的望远镜不够大、不够好。

sentences.en: It was as if we had been in the back of the room and couldn't see any details on Mars.
sentences.zh: 这就好像我们当时坐在教室的后排，根本看不清火星上的任何细节一样。

sentences.en: And then those telescopes brought us to the middle of the room where we could see there were some details, but we weren't seeing them clearly.
sentences.zh: 然后，这些望远镜把我们带到了房间中央，在那里我们可以看到一些细节，但看得并不真切。

sentences.en: And he said, when we get even better observatories, then we will move to the front of the room and know what's really there.
sentences.zh: 他说，当我们拥有更好的天文台时，我们就会走到房间的最前面，真正看清那里有什么。

sentences.en: So the small boy theory is basically the first shot across the bow at Lowell.
sentences.zh: 因此，“小男孩理论”基本上是对洛厄尔发出的第一声警示。

sentences.en: But how did he ultimately end up being taken down?
sentences.zh: 但他最终是如何垮台的呢？

sentences.en: Well, so, I mean, at some point the whole thing would have crumbled, but it was another astronomer, very much like him, interestingly,
sentences.zh: 嗯，我的意思是，在某个时间点，整个事情都会崩溃，但有趣的是，是另一位天文学家，跟他非常像，

sentences.en: another wealthy amateur who had for a time believed in the canals of Mars, who then woke up to the fact that they weren't really there.
sentences.zh: 另一位曾经一度相信火星运河富有的业余爱好者，后来猛然惊醒，发现它们其实根本不存在。

sentences.en: So his name was Eugène Michel Antoniotti.
sentences.zh: 他的名字叫欧仁·米歇尔·安东尼奥蒂。
zh_words: 欧仁·米歇尔·安东尼奥蒂

sentences.en: He was originally from Greece.
sentences.zh: 他原本来自希腊。

sentences.en: And Antoniotti had made these maps of Mars crisscrossed by the canals.
sentences.zh: 安东尼奥蒂曾绘制过这些被运河纵横交错的火星地图。

sentences.en: So he had seen them.
sentences.zh: 所以他是看到过它们的。

sentences.en: He believed in them.
sentences.zh: 他曾对此深信不疑。

sentences.en: But over time, he started to wonder if, in fact, his eyes were playing tricks on him.
sentences.zh: 但随着时间的推移，他开始怀疑，其实是不是自己的眼睛在捉弄他。

sentences.en: And so in 1909, when Mars and Earth came especially close together, Antoniotti gained access to the largest telescope in Europe, outside Paris,
sentences.zh: 因此在1909年，当火星和地球靠得特别近的时候，安东尼奥蒂得以使用巴黎郊外欧洲最大的望远镜，

sentences.en: to examine Mars on some of the days at its very closest approach.
sentences.zh: 在火星距离最近的某些日子里对其进行观测。

sentences.en: You were not going to have another good chance like this for 15 years.
sentences.zh: 在之后的15年里，你都不会再有这么好的机会了。

sentences.en: And he got incredibly lucky.
sentences.zh: 而且他极其幸运。

sentences.en: One of those nights, he was staring at Mars when the air over Paris was dead still.
sentences.zh: 在其中的一个夜晚，当巴黎上空的气流死一般平静时，他正凝视着火星。

sentences.en: It was perfect conditions for observing the planet.
sentences.zh: 那是观测这颗行星的完美条件。

sentences.en: And whereas Mars almost always is this wobbly object in the telescope, comes in and out of focus, Mars was sitting dead still.
sentences.zh: 火星在望远镜里几乎总是晃动不定、忽远忽近，而此时它却静静地一动不动。

sentences.en: He could see the planet's surface with incredible clarity.
sentences.zh: 他能够以惊人的清晰度看到行星的表面。

sentences.en: And here's this man who knew where the canals were supposed to be.
sentences.zh: 而这个人却知道运河应该在什么位置。

sentences.en: He had drawn them.
sentences.zh: 他把它们画了下来。

sentences.en: He believed in them.
sentences.zh: 他坚信它们的存在。

sentences.en: They weren't there.
sentences.zh: 但它们并不在那里。

sentences.en: Where he was supposed to see canals, instead, he saw very natural-looking features.
sentences.zh: 在他本该看到运河的地方，他看到的却是非常自然的特征。

sentences.en: So Antoniotti, for him, it really was like this vision he saw that he was now going to tell the world what was true.
sentences.zh: 因此，对安东尼奥蒂来说，这真的就像是他看到的某种愿景，他现在要向全世界宣告真相。

sentences.en: And he decided he was going to take Lowell down.
sentences.zh: 他决定把罗威尔拉下马。

sentences.en: And things began to really unravel for Lowell after that.
sentences.zh: 在那之后，罗威尔的事情开始彻底走向崩溃。

sentences.en: Even people who supported him began to just drop off very quickly, including Schiaparelli, who was the first person to describe canals on Mars.
sentences.zh: 甚至连那些支持他的人也开始迅速离去，包括斯基帕雷利，他是第一个描述火星运河的人。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: So Schiaparelli, shortly before he died in 1910, he said, you know, these lines may be perfectly natural, and I think we should stop calling them canals.
sentences.zh: 所以斯基帕雷利在1910年去世前不久说，你知道的，这些线条可能完全是自然的，我认为我们应该停止称它们为运河。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: Camille Flammari, the French astronomer who had inspired Lowell and who continued to believe there was life on Mars,
sentences.zh: 卡米尔·弗拉马里翁，这位曾激励过罗威尔并继续坚信火星上有生命的法国天文学家，

sentences.en: was backing away from the idea that these lines were anything more than natural lines of some sort or illusions.
sentences.zh: 也开始退缩，不再认为这些线条除了某种自然线条或错觉之外还有别的什么。

sentences.en: And so Lowell was really kind of the last one holding him back at this point.
sentences.zh: 所以到这个时候，罗威尔真的成了最后一个死扛到底的人。

sentences.en: He was, but he, you know, he just dug in his heels even more, which speaks to his stubbornness, to his ego.
sentences.zh: 他是的，但你知道，他只是更加固执地坚持己见，这说明了他的顽固和自我。

sentences.en: And I think sometimes there's a sense that the more intelligent you are, the more you should be able to accept what's real.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为有时人们会觉得，你越聪明，就越应该能够接受现实。

sentences.en: But in fact, intelligence can make you incredibly smart at deluding yourself.
sentences.zh: 但事实上，聪明反而能让你在自我欺骗时变得极其高明。

sentences.en: So after Antoniotti came out and said that the canals disappeared through this superior telescope, one of Lowell's arguments was the telescope was too good, it was too powerful,
sentences.zh: 因此，在安东尼奥蒂公开表示运河是通过这架更高级的望远镜消失之后，罗威尔的论点之一是望远镜太好了、太强大了，

sentences.en: and that its own power was creating illusions.
sentences.zh: 而且它自身的威力正在制造幻觉。

sentences.en: So I don't think I'm giving anything away to say there are no Martians, there never were canals on Mars.
sentences.zh: 所以我想说火星上没有火星人，火星上也从来没有过运河，这并不算剧透。

sentences.en: But as that idea started to gain some traction toward the end of Lowell's life, he never gave an inch.
sentences.zh: 但随着这种观点在罗威尔生命接近尾声时开始获得一些认同，他却从未退让过哪怕一寸。

sentences.en: He claimed to his dying day that he was this suffering genius who people might doubt, but he would someday be proven right.
sentences.zh: 他至死都坚称自己是个饱受折磨的天才，尽管人们可能会怀疑他，但他总有一天会被证明是正确的。

sentences.en: I mean, it's pretty easy to see him as a kook and a stubborn man.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，大家很容易把他看作是一个怪人和固执的人。

sentences.en: But, you know, I gather from your book, you do have charitable opinions of Lowell and his legacy.
sentences.zh: 但你知道的，从你的书中我了解到，你对洛厄尔及其遗产抱有相当宽容的看法。

sentences.en: Could you describe what you think of him in the totality?
sentences.zh: 你能全面地描述一下你对他的看法吗？

sentences.en: Well, I mean, it's actually, it's really interesting.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我的意思是，这其实真的很有趣。

sentences.en: When I went into writing this book, I thought that I was writing a cautionary tale.
sentences.zh: 当我开始写这本书的时候，我以为我写的是一个警世故事。

sentences.en: Because, in fact, to the extent people know about the canals of Mars today, it's generally remembered as one of the great blunders of science.
sentences.zh: 因为事实上，就当今人们对火星运河的了解而言，它通常被记为科学史上的一大重大失误。

sentences.en: And it was.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: It's a story about how we can fool ourselves into believing things that aren't true because we wish they were true.
sentences.zh: 这是一个关于我们如何因为渴望某些事情成真而自我欺骗、相信虚假之物的故事。

sentences.en: But it actually is also a very inspiring tale because Lowell did a lot of good.
sentences.zh: 但它实际上也是一个非常励志的故事，因为洛厄尔做了很多好事。

sentences.en: Imagination is important.
sentences.zh: 想象力很重要。

sentences.en: And Lowell had that in spades.
sentences.zh: 而洛厄尔恰恰拥有极其丰富的想象力。

sentences.en: And he really did push people to try to answer the question about what's going on on Mars.
sentences.zh: 而且他确实推动人们去寻找火星上到底发生了什么事的答案。

sentences.en: And he really did.
sentences.zh: 他的确做到了。

sentences.en: He inspired the children of that era to get excited about outer space.
sentences.zh: 他激发了那个时代的儿童对外太空的热情。

sentences.en: I mean, it's actually, it's a kind of a divide among scientists even today.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，实际上，直到今天科学家之间仍然存在这种分歧。

sentences.en: You've got those who are very conservative, who feel their job is to collect data in a very objective way.
sentences.zh: 有一类是非常保守的科学家，他们觉得自己的工作是以非常客观的方式收集数据。

sentences.en: And then you've got those who want to take the data and imagine how it all fits together into some grand theory.
sentences.zh: 还有一类是想要利用这些数据，去想象它们如何组合成某种宏大理论的科学家。

sentences.en: And both are really important in science.
sentences.zh: 这两者在科学中都非常重要。

sentences.en: You need the collectors and you need the dreamers, those who imagine what's true.
sentences.zh: 你需要收集者，也需要梦想家，也就是那些想象真相的人。

sentences.en: So I think there's a fine line between imagination in science and dreaming of what might be and getting excited about it.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为，在科学中的想象力、对可能之事的梦想以及为此兴奋之间，有一条微妙的界限。

sentences.en: But knowing when to pull back when the evidence just doesn't support that.
sentences.zh: 但关键在于当证据不支持时，要知道何时收手。

sentences.en: And that was Lowell's great fault is that he never knew when to back down.
sentences.zh: 而洛厄尔最大的过错就在于他从不知道何时退让。

sentences.en: Yeah, I think people today might look back at the Martian craze and think everyone was so naive and gullible.
sentences.zh: 是的，我想今天的人们回看当年的火星狂热时，可能会觉得每个人都那么天真和轻信。

sentences.en: But when I read your book, I found myself thinking about our world today and our fraught relationship with science and truth.
sentences.zh: 但当我读你的书时，我发现自己在思考我们当今的世界，以及我们与科学和真相之间紧张复杂的关系。

sentences.en: And so what does Lowell's story make you think of in the present day?
sentences.zh: 那么，洛厄尔的故事让你联想到了当今时代的哪些事情？

sentences.en: So much.
sentences.zh: 非常多。

sentences.en: So it was a very interesting essay written about my book in the New Republic by the Harvard legal scholar Cass Sunstein.
sentences.zh: 《新共和国》杂志上刊登了一篇关于我书的非常有趣的评论文章，作者是哈佛大学法学学者Cass Sunstein。

sentences.en: And he brought up the name of RFK Jr.
sentences.zh: 他提到了小罗伯特·F·肯尼迪的名字。

sentences.en: And I think there are interesting parallels there.
sentences.zh: 我认为其中存在着有趣的相似之处。

sentences.en: Here you have someone from one of the most famous families in Massachusetts who has now, you know, built a reputation around skepticism on vaccines.
sentences.zh: 这里有来自马萨诸塞州最著名家族之一的人，现在，你知道的，他围绕着对疫苗的怀疑建立了自己的声誉。

sentences.en: You know, most in the scientific community think this is bunk.
sentences.zh: 你知道，科学界的多数人认为这是无稽之谈。

sentences.en: You know, the very, the study that started this all that said there was a link between vaccines and autism has been shown to have been fraudulent.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，正是那项引发这一切、声称疫苗与自闭症之间存在联系的研究，已被证明是造假的。

sentences.en: And yet, RFK Jr.
sentences.zh: 然而，小罗伯特·F·肯尼迪

sentences.en: has built his identity around this idea.
sentences.zh: 却围绕这个观点建立了自己的身份认同。

sentences.en: And he's, a lot of people find him very articulate, charismatic.
sentences.zh: 而且他，很多人觉得他非常口齿伶俐、极具魅力。

sentences.en: And again, I can't speak for what's going on inside his head.
sentences.zh: 再说一次，我无法揣测他脑子里在想什么。

sentences.en: But I think one can see parallels to Percival Lowell from a prominent Massachusetts family, had a lot needed to prove that he was an important person.
sentences.zh: 但我认为，人们可以看出他与帕西瓦尔·洛厄尔有相似之处。洛厄尔来自马萨诸塞州的一个显赫家族，极力想要证明自己是个重要人物。

sentences.en: His way of doing it was this theory about life on Mars.
sentences.zh: 他证明自己的方式，就是提出这个关于火星生命的理论。

sentences.en: And even as people tried to chip away at it, he was unwilling to give an inch because that would have just crushed his ego.
sentences.zh: 即使人们试图驳倒这个理论，他也寸步不让，因为那样会彻底摧毁他的自负。

sentences.en: I mean, there's also this compulsion of having these ultimate wealthy, privileged insiders casting themselves as renegade outsiders to orthodoxy.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这些极为富有、享有特权的内部人士，总是有一种强烈的冲动，把自己塑造成对抗正统的流亡局外人。

sentences.en: What is, what is, why is that narrative so compelling?
sentences.zh: 这是为什么，为什么，为什么这种叙事如此引人入胜？

sentences.en: That's a good question, but I guess what I would say is a lot of folks in this situation cast themselves as skeptics.
sentences.zh: 这是一个好问题，但我想说的是，处在这种境况中的很多人都把自己标榜为怀疑论者。

sentences.en: And I'm all for skepticism.
sentences.zh: 而我完全支持怀疑精神。

sentences.en: Science should be built on skepticism.
sentences.zh: 科学应该建立在怀疑精神之上。

sentences.en: But I often think that it's some of those people who promote skepticism who are not skeptical enough of themselves.
sentences.zh: 但我经常认为，正是其中一些宣扬怀疑精神的人，对自己却不够怀疑。

sentences.en: We all have to have the humility to understand that we are fallible human beings who, when we latch onto an idea, are loath to give it up.
sentences.zh: 我们所有人都必须具备谦逊的态度，明白我们都是会犯错的人，一旦我们迷上某种观点，就会极其不愿放弃。

sentences.en: I mean, I've been a science journalist and writer for 40 years.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我已经当了40年的科学记者和作家。

sentences.en: Most of what science reporters report on is wrong because you're looking at the cutting edge of science.
sentences.zh: 科学记者报道的大多数内容都是错的，因为你们关注的是科学的最前沿。

sentences.en: You're at that point where something's known, but it hasn't quite been figured out.
sentences.zh: 你们正处于那种知其然而不知其所以然的阶段。

sentences.en: And people are trying to get better data and coming up with theories.
sentences.zh: 人们试图获得更好的数据，并提出各种理论。

sentences.en: And most of the time, they're wrong.
sentences.zh: 而且大多数时候，他们都是错的。

sentences.en: Eventually, we move beyond it and we can see, in hindsight, which was the right path.
sentences.zh: 最终，我们会超越这一阶段，事后回过头来，就能看出哪条才是正确的道路。

sentences.en: It happens all the time, but it doesn't usually happen on quite so grand a scale as it did with Percival Lowell.
sentences.zh: 这种情况时常发生，但通常不像帕西瓦尔·洛厄尔那次规模那么宏大。

sentences.en: Well, David Barron, thank you so much for talking with me.
sentences.zh: 好的，大卫·巴伦，非常感谢你和我交谈。

sentences.en: I just had a blast reading your book and a blast talking with you.
sentences.zh: 我读你的书时感到非常开心，和你交谈也很痛快。

sentences.en: It was so much fun.
sentences.zh: 真的非常有趣。

sentences.en: Well, Robin, it was my pleasure.
sentences.zh: 罗宾，这是我的荣幸。

sentences.en: And with a last name like yours, I figure it was bound to be that I would come on your show.
sentences.zh: 而且凭你这样的姓氏，我想我注定是要来你的节目的。

sentences.en: Makes sense to me.
sentences.zh: 我也这么觉得。
